full_judgment: 24. Mr. Miah Abdul Gafur, the learned Advocate for the appellant, referred to the case of Sekander Ali and another Vs. The Crown, reported in DLR-1950(Vol.2)-158, as discussed by my learned brother. In that case, the appellant was charged for under Section 302/109 of the Bangladesh Penal Code for abetting some known principals who were co-accused with him but were acquitted. The appellant was however, convicted under Section 302/109 of the Bangladesh Penal Code for abetting some unknown murderers, by altering the charge. Their Lordships held that the conviction of the appellant of that case for abetting unknown persons after the failure of the charge of abetment of known persons, cannot be sustained. The facts of that case are different from the facts of the present case. In my opinion, in the present case, the charge under Section 302/109 of the Bangladesh Penal Code is proper and not illegal the appellant could be convicted on the charge, if there was evidence. But as there is no evidence to prove the charge, the order of conviction is not justified.
